data.gender_notes: Devilaal is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devi-lāl, derived from Devi (Goddess) and Lāl (God of Gods), represents divine grace, power, and protection. The name Devilaal carries the meaning “God of Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devilaal usually hope their child will grow to embody god of gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Devilaal belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Gods.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devilaal total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Devilaal" originates from the rich Indian history, where the divine is deeply engrained in every aspect of life. The prefix "Devi" symbolizes the worship of Goddesses, which is a significant part of Hindu culture. The suffix "Lāl" referencing Lord Shiva, the supreme God, further emphasizes the importance of divine connection and reverence. Using this powerful name to identify an individual is a constant reminder of the divine importance of human existence and serves to instill a sense of sacredness and godliness in everyday life.
data.spiritual_significance: This name "Devilaal" symbolizes the personal connection to the divine and invokes a sublime spiritual significance. It is a name that celebrates the grace and power of the Goddess and the majesty of the God of Gods- a reflection of their presence in every aspect of life. It underscores the rooted faith in the supreme power and offers protection, wisdom, and guidance to the bearer of this name. The name Devilaal instills a deep sense of devotion, respect, and awe towards the divine, reminding the individual to live a god-centered life constantly.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Devilaal signifies the divine protection and guidance of the deity, Deva. It embodies the idea of being God-fearing and seeking the blessings of the divine for strength and wisdom in life.

historical_references.reference: Devilaal is believed to be a local forms of the name of the Hindu god Indra, who was the king of the devas in ancient Indian mythology. Indra was the god of rain, thunderbolts, and war. He was one of the most important deities in the early Hindu pantheon, and his cult dates back to at least the 2nd millennium BCE.

Another reference suggests that Devilaal may be a regional variant of the name of the Hindu god Vishnu, who is one of the principal deities of Hinduism. Vishnu is the preserver of the universe in Hinduism, and is known to have assumed various incarnations or avatars to save the world from evil. The name Devilaal could be a local pronunciation or corrupted form of the name of Vishnu, particularly in regions where his cult was prominent.
